title: Meaning and synonym in context
summary: Infer a word's meaning in its exact sentence, then choose a replacement that preserves its sense, grammatical role and strength.

sections.title: Keep the sentence meaning steady
content: Compare: “The notes were careful” and “The notes were cautiously.” Only careful can replace a describing word after were. A synonym must preserve grammar as well as general meaning.
For each target word, name its word class and predict a plain meaning before looking at any options.

sections.title: Use Frame, Clues, Precision and Substitute
content: Frame: read the whole sentence and identify the target word's grammatical job. Notice whether it names, describes, modifies or shows an action.
Clues: read the sentence before and after it. Look for definitions, examples, contrast, cause, result and repeated ideas.
Precision: predict a short meaning, then compare each option's strength, tone and usual use. Near-synonyms can differ in an important way.
Substitute: place the candidate in the original sentence. Reject it if the sentence becomes ungrammatical or changes what the writer claims.

sections.title: Resolve one word from its passage role
content: Example: “The committee made a tentative decision and promised to review it after the trial.” The promise to review the decision shows that tentative means provisional or not yet final.
Temporary is related but focuses on duration. Nervous describes a feeling. Provisional matches the decision's status and remains an adjective in the same sentence frame.
The correct replacement must pass all three tests: contextual sense, grammatical role and degree of certainty.

sections.title: Mark the evidence around the word
content: Box the target word, underline its sentence frame and bracket the clue that supports your prediction. Then label the predicted word class.
When the question asks for a word from the passage, copy only the exact word. When it asks for a replacement, test the option inside the full original sentence.

sections.title: Use nearby and wider context
content: Start with the target sentence, but expand to the surrounding paragraph when local clues are incomplete. A later example or result may confirm the intended meaning.
Ignore meanings that the word can have elsewhere if they do not fit this passage. Writers select one sense of a word at a time.

sections.title: Diagnose an imprecise replacement
content: Dictionary-first trap: I chose a familiar meaning without checking this sentence.
Word-class mismatch: my option changed a noun, verb, adjective or adverb into the wrong form.
Strength or tone shift: my option made the claim stronger, weaker or more emotional.
Clue-range error: I stopped at one sentence even though the paragraph supplied the deciding evidence. Record one cause before correcting the answer.

sections.title: Voices from the river town
content: Resolve six contextual meanings in one original five-paragraph passage. All responses are marked together so early feedback cannot reveal later answers.
